key_insight: Algebraic World Model turns interactions with unfamiliar environments into executable mathematical models and Lean 4 proofs of reachability or impossibility.
engineering_relevance: The framework links exploratory agents with formal verification, enabling inspectable rules and machine-checked guarantees relative to a learned environment model.
method: Explore environments and iteratively test and revise executable Python hypotheses.
Organize hypotheses into typed objects and shared rules, then simplify using category-theory-guided transformations.
Formalize the resulting model in Lean 4 to verify winning trajectories and prove impossibility.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports kernel-checked impossibility proofs in all six runs across two impossible levels, versus none in twelve baseline runs, and Lean replay of winning trajectories for all 183 levels across 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games.
watch_item: Proofs certify conclusions within the learned model; their applicability to the actual environment depends on whether its inferred rules capture all relevant behavior.
paper_title: Algebraic World Model: From Exploration to Proofs
